featured.title: Strait of Hormuz Disruption Raises Global Energy Security Concerns
featured.content: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to its lowest level in more than two months following a surge in attacks on tankers. Kpler data analysed by Reuters showed only seven commodity vessels passed through the waterway on Tuesday, while crude volumes fell to about 10.1 million barrels per day, around 74% of pre-war levels. Reuters reports that alternative exports from the Gulf of Oman and Red Sea have partly offset the reduction, but the disruption remains a major concern for energy markets and global trade.

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Falls Sharply as Tanker Attacks Intensify
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz recorded its lowest vessel traffic in more than two months on Tuesday. Kpler data showed seven commodity vessels passed through the strait, while crude volumes fell to about 10.1 million barrels per day. Before the conflict, around 125 large commercial vessels crossed the waterway each day, carrying shipments equivalent to roughly 20% of global oil and fuel supplies. Alternative routes are helping offset some of the shortfall, but shipping risks remain elevated.

articles.title: Oil Returns Above $100 as Middle East Shipping Risks Grow
articles.content: Brent crude rose to about $101.53 a barrel in early Thursday trading, while US West Texas Intermediate reached approximately $89.39. The latest rise follows increased attacks on shipping around the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. The International Energy Agency is accelerating the release of previously announced strategic oil stocks and prioritising diesel supplies as governments respond to tight fuel markets.

articles.title: ISWAP Attack Kills Nigerian Soldiers in Borno
articles.content: Islamic State West Africa Province militants attacked a Nigerian military base in the Kukawa area of Borno State. Nigerian authorities said troops repelled the attack and killed more than 25 militants. A senior military officer told the Associated Press that 10 Nigerian soldiers were killed. The attack highlights the continuing security challenge posed by armed extremist groups in northeastern Nigeria.

articles.title: Zamfara Security Situation Under Investigation After Reported Military Camp Attack
articles.content: A separate security incident has been reported in Bindin, Zamfara State, where gunmen reportedly attacked a military camp. Reports have also circulated about heavy civilian casualties involving small-scale gold miners. The reported civilian death toll had not been independently confirmed at the time of publication. RadiantWaves Media will continue to distinguish confirmed casualty figures from reports that remain under verification.

articles.title: Nigerian Air Force Confirms 25 Dead in Ondo Aircraft Crash
articles.content: The Nigerian Air Force has confirmed that 25 people died when an ATR-42 military aircraft crashed in Ondo State on Monday while travelling from Benin City to Lagos. The aircraft had five crew members and 20 passengers, according to the Air Force. President Bola Tinubu ordered an investigation and declared three days of national mourning. Earlier reports had cited a higher figure, but the official Air Force figure is now 25.

articles.title: France Student Protests Continue as Government Suspends Stun Grenade Use
articles.content: Nationwide student protests in France are continuing for a third week amid complaints about deteriorating school infrastructure, teacher shortages, overcrowding and education funding. Reuters reports that more than 500 schools have been closed or affected. The government has suspended the use of stun grenades in policing the student movement after a 15-year-old boy lost his hand during a confrontation in Lens. Investigations into police incidents are continuing, while further demonstrations are planned.

articles.title: Wall Street Pulls Back as Treasury Yields Reach Multi-Decade High
articles.content: US stocks retreated on Wednesday after recently reaching record levels. The S&P 500 fell 0.2%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped about 341 points and the Nasdaq declined 0.2%. The US 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.36%, its highest level since 2002. Higher borrowing costs, elevated oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty are increasing pressure across financial markets.

articles.title: AI Investment Boom Drives New Wave of Corporate Borrowing
articles.content: Major technology companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Reuters reports that Broadcom is pursuing about $50 billion in financing, while SpaceX plans approximately $30 billion in bonds and another $10 billion in loans. The borrowing is adding pressure to credit markets and raising questions about the financial risks surrounding the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

articles.title: France's Fiscal Concerns Continue to Weigh on the Euro
articles.content: Financial markets remain focused on France's public finances and political uncertainty. The euro has recently fallen to a 17-month low against the US dollar, while French government bond yields have remained elevated. Investors are closely monitoring the country's budget situation and the wider implications for euro-zone financial stability.

articles.title: IEA Accelerates Oil Stock Releases as Diesel Supplies Tighten
articles.content: The International Energy Agency has agreed to accelerate the release of oil stocks under its existing emergency programme and prioritise diesel supplies where possible. Around 100 million barrels from previously announced releases have yet to reach markets. The move comes as the Iran conflict and disruptions to tanker traffic contribute to record fuel prices and tight diesel supplies.

articles.title: Global Markets Face Pressure From Oil, Bonds and AI Debt
articles.content: Global investors are navigating several simultaneous pressures: higher oil prices, elevated government bond yields, concerns over public finances and increasing corporate borrowing to fund artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Asian shares were broadly weaker Thursday, while the dollar strengthened and European financial markets remained sensitive to developments in France and the Middle East.

morningSummary: This morning's global picture is dominated by energy security, the continuing Middle East conflict, Nigeria's security situation, France's student protests and pressure across financial markets. The sharp reduction in Strait of Hormuz traffic is particularly significant because the waterway is a major global energy route. At the same time, Nigeria is dealing with fresh military casualties and a deadly aircraft crash, while France faces continued disruption from student demonstrations.
bigQuestion: When security and economic pressures rise at the same time, what should governments prioritise first — protecting people, protecting the economy, or finding a balance between both?
